title: Heuristic-weighted rerank evaluation with latency slices
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: We currently run uniform-sampled rerank evals and instrument NDCG/MRR at a service level but lack stable stratification by observed latency and by customer prompt-set frequency. This makes it hard to reason about quality regressions that only appear at low-latency operating points or in low-frequency customer promptsets.

Goal: Build an offline + online evaluation harness that: (1) computes NDCG@5 / MRR@10 per-customer-promptset, (2) applies heuristic-weighted sampling to upweight rare but high-impact promptsets and production tail queries, and (3) slices metrics by latency buckets (p50/p95/p99 and bucketed ranges) so we can measure quality/latency trade-offs for model variants and quantization profiles.

Success metrics:
- Automated NDCG@5 and MRR@10 reporting per-customer-promptset for the top 500 promptset ids within 24 hours of ingestion.
- Latency-sliced NDCG/MRR (buckets: <50ms, 50-150ms, 150-500ms, >500ms) surfaced in dashboard and alertable when delta > 2.5% compared to baseline.
- A/B experiment hooks implemented so that both traffic and offline ground-truth labels are attributed to experiment arms; experiment latency/quality trade-off graphs available in console.

Approach:
1) Sampling & weighting: implement a configurable sampler that combines three signals into a sampling weight: (a) promptset frequency inverse (upweight rare promptsets), (b) recent relative error-rate (upweight promptsets where reranker changed user behavior), and (c) production latency percentile (upweight tail latencies). Provide a simple heuristic formula in code with feature flags for ablation.
2) Latency slicing: add a small telemetry tuple to rerank response events (observed_server_ms, model_decode_ms, routing_ms). These are lightweight integers; we will use them to assign the request to latency buckets when computing offline metrics.
3) Instrumentation and A/B hooks: extend existing AB hook to tag evaluation logs with experiment_id and arm. Ensure offline label ingestion preserves the arm. Implement a storage layout for evaluation traces (sharded by date + promptset_id) optimized for fast joins.
4) Offline pipeline: new dag in ranking-evals that consumes evaluation traces, computes per-promptset NDCG/MRR and per-latency-bucket aggregates, and writes results to metrics store and a long-term parquet for retro analysis.
5) Dashboarding & alerting: Grafana panel for per-customer-promptset NDCG/MRR and latency-sliced graphs, Prometheus metrics for drift/quality-regression alerts.

Trade-offs considered:
- Complexity vs interpretability: weighted sampling yields faster detection of regressions in rare promptsets but makes population-level numbers harder to interpret. We will ship both: uniform baseline + weighted signal.
- Storage cost vs query speed: storing full traces for every rerank request is expensive. We will sample at ingestion (configurable) and rely on the weighted sampler to increase retention for upweighted promptsets.
- Latency attribution accuracy: server-side timestamps are noisy for cross-region routing. We add model_decode_ms to isolate model execution latency from network/routing.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Week 1 (this ticket): implement sampler, telemetry fields, and small schema change for evaluation traces. Add feature flags.
- Week 2: offline DAG + unit tests; small job to backfill last 30 days for validation; open initial PR.
- Week 3: dashboard panels and A/B wiring; run internal canary experiment on 5% traffic for 72h.
- Week 4: iterate on thresholds and alert rules; include PM/UX review for console exposure.

Acceptance criteria:
- PR merged with sampler and telemetry changes and feature-flag gate.
- Offline pipeline computes and stores per-promptset NDCG@5 & MRR@10 with latency buckets for last 7 days.
- Grafana panel demonstrates a visible latency-sliced NDCG delta for a synthetic regression run.
- Documentation: Confluence page with sampling formula and how to interpret weighted vs uniform metrics.

Risks & mitigation:
- Metric confusion: will ship both uniform and weighted signals with headers and docs.
- False positives in alerts due to sampling noise: require 6-hour sustained delta before firing high-severity alerts.

updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with PM (Jenna Kim) and Design (Maya Chen). Agreed to ship sampler behind flag and keep both uniform and weighted signals.
2026-03-03: Schema proposal posted to #eng-ranking channel; brief review from infra (Diego Ramos) asking for backwards-compatible trace layout.
2026-03-05: Prototype sampler landed in feature branch; unit tests added. Sampler exposes three weights and a normalization hook.
2026-03-06: Telemetry fields added: observed_server_ms, model_decode_ms, routing_ms. Small PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/2317
2026-03-07: Spike to backfill 30 days ran; noticed high storage growth for very low-frequency promptsets. Decided to cap retention for promptsets with <10 queries/day unless upweighted.
2026-03-08: PM feedback: add a 'customer-visible' translation for weighted metrics so support teams can explain anomalies. Added as doc action item.
2026-03-09: Opened offline DAG branch in ranking-evals repo; preliminary compute shows weighted NDCG detects synthetic regression 2x faster than uniform sampling.
2026-03-10: Security review requested for telemetry fields — security asked to confirm no PII in promptset ids. Marked security_review_required=false after confirmation by Security (Arjun Singh).
